issues.legal_issue: A court must decide a pending application seeking permission to file one appeal against a common judgment and separate decrees before dismissing the appeal on a preliminary objection to its maintainability.
material_facts: Two suits concerning the same passage were consolidated and disposed of by one common judgment, with separate decrees drawn in each suit.
The appellant filed one first appeal challenging both decrees and applied for permission to proceed by a single appeal.
The High Court admitted the appeal, directed the parties to file responses to the permission application, but left that application undecided.

The High Court later dismissed the appeal on a preliminary maintainability objection and res judicata without deciding the permission application, thereby preventing the appellant from seeking an opportunity to cure the procedural defect.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s dismissal could not stand because it had not decided the pending permission application. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and remanded the matter, directing the High Court to decide that application before the preliminary maintainability objection.
issues.legal_principle: Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for an appeal from a decree, and a first appeal is a valuable right in which questions of fact and law may be reconsidered. A procedural defect that may be an irregularity capable of cure should not defeat a litigant’s substantive right without a reasonable opportunity to address it. The judgment expressed no opinion on the correctness of the High Court’s res judicata findings and relied on no earlier case for this ruling.

rule.if: first_appeal_from_consolidated_suits and single_appeal_permission_pending and appeal_dismissed_on_maintainability_without_deciding_permission and procedural_defect_could_be_cured

predicates.first_appeal_from_consolidated_suits: A litigant brought a first appeal challenging decrees entered in separate suits that had been consolidated and disposed of by a common judgment.
predicates.single_appeal_permission_pending: The appellant had asked the appellate court for permission to proceed with one appeal against the common judgment and separate decrees, and that request remained undecided.
predicates.appeal_dismissed_on_maintainability_with: The appellate court dismissed the appeal on a preliminary maintainability objection before deciding the pending request for permission.
predicates.procedural_defect_could_be_cured: The procedural defect could potentially have been corrected if the litigant had been given an opportunity to do so.

issues.definition: When a first appeal concerns decrees from consolidated suits and a request to proceed by one appeal remains pending, dismissal on maintainability grounds without deciding that request must be set aside if the procedural defect could have been cured.
